# pai providers

List providers (● = active); `providers use NAME` switches

```
pai providers [command] [options]
```

Shows every provider you can start a session on, its default model, and how much of its quota is used when that is known.
● marks the active provider.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--json` | flag | — | Machine-readable JSON output |

```sh
pai providers
pai providers --json
pai providers use glm
```

See also: `pai new`, `pai open`, `pai providers use`

### pai providers use

Make a provider the active one

```
pai providers use NAME [options]
```

The active provider is where `pai new` starts and where new workers go by default. Classes pinned to a provider are re-pointed.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `NAME` | yes | Provider name from `pai providers` |

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | flag | — | Print the exec line instead of executing |

```sh
pai providers use glm
pai providers use anthropic
```

See also: `pai providers`, `pai new`

### pai providers add

Add a provider (the first one also turns workers on)

```
pai providers add NAME [options]
```

Adds a provider that workers can run on. The first provider you add also turns workers on and sets up the default classes.
Give the API token with --key (stored in workers.yaml, file kept private) or --key-file (path to a private file holding it), not both.
OpenAI-style APIs: --protocol openai --upstream-url URL (runs through the local proxy).
ChatGPT plan through the Codex CLI: --engine codex. Image generation: --engine image.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `NAME` | yes | Name for the new provider, e.g. glm |

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--base-url URL` | string | — | Anthropic-compatible API base URL (required unless --protocol openai) |
| `--url URL` | string | — | Same as --base-url |
| `--model ID` | string | — | Default model id for this provider (required) |
| `--key TOKEN` | string | — | API token, written into workers.yaml; use instead of --key-file |
| `--key-file PATH` | string | — | File holding the API token (kept private); leave out for a local server |
| `--fast-model ID` | string | — | Cheaper model for quick checks and routing |
| `--env NAME=VALUE` | string | — | Extra environment variable for runs (repeat for several) |
| `--note TEXT` | string | — | Short note shown in the provider list |
| `--protocol KIND` | string | — | anthropic (default) or openai |
| `--upstream-url URL` | string | — | Chat Completions base URL (required for --protocol openai) |
| `--engine KIND` | string | — | claude (default), codex, or image |
| `--context-window TOKENS` | number | — | Context window for the usage meter (default 200000) |
| `--quota-probe URL` | string | — | URL whose JSON first number is the quota percent (0-100) |
| `--cost-tier 1-5` | string | — | Cost tier: 1 (cheapest) to 5 (most expensive; default 3) |
| `--tags LIST` | string | — | Capability tags, comma-separated (from: code, vision, image-gen, long-context, fast, reasoning) |

```sh
pai worker providers add glm --url https://api.example.invalid/anthropic --key-file ~/glm.key --model glm-5.3 --fast-model glm-5.3-flash
pai worker providers add local --protocol openai --upstream-url http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1 --model qwen
```

See also: `pai worker providers use`, `pai worker providers list`

### pai providers update

Change a provider's cost tier and tags

```
pai providers update NAME [options]
```

Routing constraints (--max-cost-tier, --require-tags on a class) look at these two settings.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `NAME` | yes | Provider to change |

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--cost-tier 1-5` | string | — | Cost tier: 1 (cheapest) to 5 (most expensive; default 3) |
| `--tags LIST` | string | — | Capability tags, comma-separated (from: code, vision, image-gen, long-context, fast, reasoning); --tags '' clears them |

```sh
pai worker providers update glm --cost-tier 2
pai worker providers update glm --tags long-context,reasoning
```

See also: `pai worker providers list`

### pai providers remove

Remove a provider and the classes pointing at it

```
pai providers remove NAME
```

Deletes the provider from workers.yaml. Classes pinned to it are removed too.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `NAME` | yes | Provider to remove |

```sh
pai worker providers remove glm
pai worker providers list
```

See also: `pai worker providers add`

### pai providers enable

Turn a provider on (also clears its cooldown)

```
pai providers enable NAME
```

Makes the provider usable again and clears any cooldown after hitting a limit.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `NAME` | yes | Provider name |

```sh
pai worker providers enable glm
pai worker providers list
```

See also: `pai worker providers disable`

### pai providers disable

Turn a provider off (automatic routing skips it)

```
pai providers disable NAME
```

Automatic routing skips a disabled provider. Naming it with --provider still works.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `NAME` | yes | Provider name |

```sh
pai worker providers disable glm
pai worker providers list
```

See also: `pai worker providers enable`

### pai providers test

Send one word through a provider to check it answers

```
pai providers test [NAME]
```

Sends a tiny prompt and prints the reply and the time it took. Exits 1 if the provider does not answer. Without a name it tests the active provider.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `NAME` | no | Provider to test (default: the active one) |

```sh
pai worker providers test
pai worker providers test glm
```

See also: `pai worker providers list`
